page: Amazon Web Services g7e.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, designed for graphics-intensive applications and machine learning inference. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8559C processor providing 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores at a 2.4 GHz base frequency, supported by 320 MB of L3 cache and hardware acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes 128 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Hardware acceleration is driven by an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPU featuring 96 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local high-speed storage is integrated directly via a 1900 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 50 Gbps baseline networking interface. This architectural pairing of extensive VRAM, fast local NVMe storage, and high-throughput networking facilitates low-latency data staging and large parameter handling without saturating system bus interfaces.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional capacity in generative AI workloads, registering top-decile performance across prompt processing and text generation for small (135M), medium (7B), and large (70B) language models. Text generation reaches 31.01 tokens per second on 70B parameter models and 222.31 tokens per second on 7B models. General compute benchmarks reflect top-tier single-core Geekbench ratings alongside solid single-threaded compression throughput, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth results align with expected median levels for 16-vCPU allocations.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, bundling 96 GB of GPU VRAM with dense DDR5 memory and local NVMe storage provides a cost-effective alternative to multi-GPU clusters for workloads requiring substantial model footprints. Tradeoffs include standard multi-core CPU throughput that matches average mid-range tiers, making the instance specialized primarily for accelerator-dependent tasks rather than general compute-heavy batches. Primary operational fits include large language model inference, AI image synthesis, 3D rendering pipelines, and data-intensive visual computing.
